title: Chemical Changes: Physical vs Chemical Changes and Word Equations Basics
subject: Science

questions.question: Which of the following is a physical change?
questions.explanation: Melting ice is a physical change because water changes from solid to liquid state, but it is still water. No new substance is formed.

questions.question: Which observation is the BEST evidence that a chemical change has occurred?
options: The substance changes from solid to liquid
The substance becomes smaller in size
A new gas is produced that was not present before
questions.explanation: The production of a new gas indicates that new substances have been formed, which is definitive evidence of a chemical change.

questions.question: Which of the following is a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Burning paper produces ash and smoke, which are new substances with different properties from the original paper.

questions.question: In a word equation, where are the reactants written?
options: On the right side of the arrow
On the left side of the arrow
questions.explanation: Reactants are the starting substances in a chemical reaction and are written on the left side of the arrow.

questions.question: In a word equation, where are the products written?
options: On the left side of the arrow
On the right side of the arrow
questions.explanation: Products are the new substances formed in a chemical reaction and are written on the right side of the arrow.

questions.question: What does the arrow (→) in a word equation represent?
options: The reactants are equal to the products
The reactants change to form the products
The reaction can proceed in both directions
The products are more important than the reactants
questions.explanation: The arrow in a word equation means 'reacts to form' or 'produces'. It shows the direction of the chemical change from reactants to products.

questions.question: Magnesium burns in air to form magnesium oxide. Which substance is the reactant?
questions.explanation: Magnesium is a reactant (starting substance). Oxygen from air is also a reactant. Magnesium oxide is the product formed.

questions.question: Iron burns in air to form iron oxide. Which substance is the product?
questions.explanation: Iron oxide is the product (new substance formed). Iron and oxygen are the reactants.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a physical change?
options: New substances are formed with different properties
The substance changes form but no new substance is formed
The change cannot be reversed under any conditions
questions.explanation: A physical change involves a change in form, state, or appearance, but the substance itself remains the same. No new substances are formed.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a chemical change?
options: One or more new substances with different properties are formed
The substance changes state but remains the same substance
The change can always be easily reversed
Only the size of the substance changes
questions.explanation: A chemical change involves the formation of new substances with different properties from the original substances.

questions.question: Water freezes to form ice. Is this a physical or chemical change?
questions.explanation: Freezing water is a physical change. Water changes from liquid to solid state, but it is still water. No new substance is formed.

questions.question: Iron reacts with oxygen to form rust. Which one of the following cannot prevent rusting?
options: Cover the iron with a layer of metal by electroplating
Coat the iron with a layer of plastic
Place the iron in a wooden container that is not airtight
questions.explanation: Iron reacts with oxygen in the presence of water to form rust.

questions.question: In the word equation: hydrogen + oxygen → water, which substances are the reactants?
questions.explanation: Reactants are written on the left side of the arrow. Hydrogen and oxygen are the starting substances that react to form water.

questions.question: In the word equation: hydrogen + oxygen → water, which substance is the product?
questions.explanation: Products are written on the right side of the arrow. Water is the new substance formed from hydrogen and oxygen.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT evidence of a chemical change?
options: A precipitate (solid) forms when two solutions are mixed
questions.explanation: Melting is a physical change (change of state). The substance remains the same chemically. Colour change, gas production, and precipitate formation are evidence of chemical changes.

questions.question: A student heats sugar in a test tube. The sugar melts, then turns brown and finally black, producing a smell. Which statement is correct?
options: Only physical changes occurred because the sugar melted
Only chemical changes occurred because the colour changed
Neither physical nor chemical changes occurred
Both physical and chemical changes occurred
questions.explanation: Melting is a physical change (state change). The browning and blackening with a new smell indicate chemical changes where new substances are formed.

questions.question: Which word equation correctly shows the reactants and products for burning magnesium?
questions.explanation: Magnesium and oxygen are the reactants (left side). Magnesium oxide is the product (right side). The arrow shows the direction of the reaction.

questions.question: Salt dissolves in water. Is this a physical or chemical change?
questions.explanation: Dissolving salt in water is a physical change. The salt can be recovered by evaporating the water. No new substance is formed.

questions.question: Which of the following changes can be easily reversed?
questions.explanation: Melting ice can be easily reversed by freezing the water back to ice. Burning, rusting, and cooking are chemical changes that are difficult or impossible to reverse.

questions.question: What is the main difference between reactants and products in a chemical reaction?
options: Reactants are formed during the reaction; products are used up
Products are always solids; reactants are always liquids or gases
Reactants and products are always the same substances
Reactants are the starting substances; products are the new substances formed
questions.explanation: Reactants are the substances present before the reaction starts. Products are the new substances formed as a result of the chemical change. They have different properties from the reactants.
